explain_en: 그런 points to something the other person just said or something already mentioned. Use 그런 for things in the conversation and 저런 for things you can see far away.

dis.h: that kind; thing just mentioned or near you

p.n: 그런 means the kind of person you just mentioned. 저런 means the kind of person over there.

examples.en: Restaurants like that one are good.
Where do you buy clothes like that?
I want to buy a bag like that one over there.
I want to work in a big building like that.
I've never seen a person like that.

explain: 저런은 말하는 사람과 듣는 사람이 둘 다 보는, 멀리 있는 것에 써요. 이야기 속의 것에는 ‘그런’을 써요.

explain_en: 저런 is for something far away that both speaker and listener can see. For something that came up in the conversation, use 그런.

dis.h: that kind; thing far from both, visible

p.n: 저런 points at someone visible and far away. 그런 refers to someone mentioned or near the listener.

contract: 이것은 → 이건, 이것이 → 이게, 이것을 → 이걸 (그것·저것도 같아요)

contract_en: shortened in speech: 이것은 → 이건, 이것이 → 이게, 이것을 → 이걸 (그것 and 저것 work the same way)

dis.h: standard full form, also used in writing

p.n: Same meaning; 거 is the casual spoken shortening.

explain_en: 아무 is usually followed by 도 or 나. 아무도 + a negative means “no one at all”, and 아무나 means “anyone”.

p.n: 하등 is formal and literary and only goes with a negative; 아무 is neutral and also works in 아무나, 아무도.
